detail:
Why Intel Stock Popped Today

Trade Intel on Coinbase

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) climbed 9% on Thursday as reports of potential memory-chip manufacturing at its Ohio site continued to draw investor attention.

The discussions involve SK Hynix, which is considering ways to produce memory chips in the United States. One possibility would involve using part of Intel's planned Ohio manufacturing complex, while another could involve a broader venture with Intel and cloud companies.

For Intel, such an arrangement could provide another potential use for capacity at the Ohio project, which has faced delays. Reuters reported that the company has been under financial pressure as it works to expand its manufacturing operations.

Intel has not confirmed any agreement and declined to comment on speculation, while saying it remains committed to preparing the Ohio site. SK Hynix also said no specific arrangement had been finalized.

Intel shares gained 4% on Wednesday following the initial report and were trading higher again Thursday. The talks come as demand for memory chips rises alongside investment in artificial intelligence and data centers.

title: Intel Stock Jumps 4% on SK Hynix Rumor, But Here’s Why the Real Win Is Years Away
detail:
Intel Stock Jumps 4% on SK Hynix Rumor, But Here’s Why the Real Win Is Years Away
Omor Ibne Ehsan

SKHY

9984.T

INTC jumped 4% on SK Hynix lease talks, but Intel Foundry still posts $2.1B quarterly losses on just $293M in external customer revenue.

NVDA's $5B and SoftBank's $2B back Intel's U.S. fab strategy, yet INTC trades at a forward P/E of 53 with Ohio years from opening.

Read More: Avoid these 13 retirement mistakes before they derail your future (sponsor)

Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) climbed 4.03% Wednesday to close at $101.05 after reports surfaced that SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) is in early discussions with the company about producing memory chips inside the United States for the first time.

Shutterstock
INTC Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.

What's being reported is narrower than the headline suggests. CNBC's Kristina Partsinevelos described two possible structures: leasing part of the long-delayed Ohio complex, or a joint venture with Intel and large cloud buyers to anchor domestic memory supply. Neither arrangement has been signed, and Intel has not confirmed the substance of the talks.

The market response makes sense only if you read it as a vote on a strategic gap Intel has been unable to close on its own. The Foundry business generated $5.8 billion in Q2 revenue while posting a $2.1 billion operating loss, and outside customers contributed only $293 million of that total.

A named external anchor, memory or otherwise, would be the first genuine validation of a strategy that has consumed capital for years. The stock has already run 299.88% over the past year, so the question is whether an unsigned report of a facility that opens years from now deserves further re-rating.

Why a Paying Tenant Matters More Than a Partner

An idle fab is one of the most expensive assets a semiconductor company can carry. Depreciation begins whether or not wafers move, and finance costs on tools ordered years in advance accrue against no offsetting revenue.

detail:
Micron Jumps 5% as Intel CEO Says Memory Prices Have Surged Over 500%
Micron Jumps 5% as Intel CEO Says Memory Prices Have Surged Over 500%
Daragh Thomas

Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) jumped more than 5% Thursday as memory stocks rallied, two days after Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC) CEO Lip-Bu Tan warned that the memory shortage could worsen next year.

Barron's reported that Tan's comments helped drive the move. SK hynix Inc. (NASDAQ:SKHY) also gained about 5%, while the Nasdaq rose more than 1% as the broader market rallied following Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision.

Micron reports fiscal fourth-quarter results Sept. 30, when investors will get the next read on whether the memory shortage is still pushing prices and margins higher.

Prediction traders remain bullish on the AI spending cycle supporting memory demand. Polymarket gives Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) about a 71% chance of ending 2026 as the world's largest company, with more than $7 million traded.

That matters for Micron because Nvidia's AI accelerators require large amounts of high-bandwidth memory, one of the tightest parts of the memory market. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said in June that supply should improve only gradually in 2028.

Tan Says Memory Pressure Could Worsen in 2027

Tan made the comments Tuesday at the AI Infrastructure Summit in Santa Clara.

Memory chip prices have climbed between five and seven times as limited supply struggles to keep pace with AI demand, Tan said. He added that the bottleneck could worsen next year.

The warning echoes concerns across the memory industry. SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung told Reuters in July that 2027 would be the worst year in the industry's history for supply.

TrendForce estimates server DRAM contract prices rose 64% in the second half of 2025 and could climb another 270% during 2026. Compounded, that would put prices at roughly six times their mid-2025 level by the end of 2026.

Why 2027 Matters for Micron

Micron is already turning tight supply into sharply higher profits. Fiscal third-quarter revenue reached $41.46 billion, up from $9.30 billion a year earlier, while non-GAAP gross margin hit 84.9%. The company guided to roughly $50 billion in fourth-quarter revenue and an 86% gross margin.

Micron said in June that 14 of its first 16 strategic customer agreements carried about $100 billion in minimum contracted revenue. The agreements use price bands designed to give Micron and customers more visibility through the memory cycle.

High prices can eventually curb demand and encourage additional capacity. TrendForce nevertheless expects memory pricing to remain elevated in 2027 even as new supply comes online.

Wednesday's rate hike knocked more than 630 points off the Dow. Thursday morning, Wall Street decided it had overreacted, and chip stocks led the apology tour.

The Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC) rose 1.4% as of 11:24 a.m. ET, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) added 0.9%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES: ^DJI) gained 0.4%. Twenty of the Dow's 30 components traded higher at this moment.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

^IXIC data by YCharts

Chips did the heavy lifting again

Speaking at a tech conference, Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) CEO Lip-Bu Tan said his company can only meet 50% of CPU demand due to limited manufacturing capacity and a shortage of memory chips. He also accelerated the ramp-up of new manufacturing nodes, and a couple of analysts posted bullish reports on the stock. Intel is up 8.6% on a bundle of news that also boosted memory makers.

I don't know that investors needed another reminder of soaring memory prices, but there you go. Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) is up 5.8%, and SK Hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY) rose 3.9%.

Other chip stocks tagged along. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) rose 2.5% and was the biggest single boost to both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) gained 6.2%.

Image source: Getty Images.

The macro backdrop cooperated for once. The 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 5 basis points to 4.949%, dropping back under the 5% level it crossed on Wednesday. The oil sector also relaxed on reports that Saudi Arabia will supply more crude to Asian refiners through ship-to-ship transfers near Oman's Sohar port. U.S. crude slipped about 1% to roughly $100 a barrel and Brent fell 2% to about $102.

The Dow's smaller gain largely rested on one stock with close ties to the AI data center construction trade. Caterpillar (NYSE: CAT) rose 1.9% and contributed 89 Dow points, more than twice the next-largest contribution.

Sixteen of eighteen Fed officials want another hike this year

Wednesday's decision lifted the federal funds target range to 3.75% to 4% on a unanimous 12-0 vote. Most market analysts had expected a dissent or two, but this was a clean all-in vote.

That's not the end of the Fed story, though. The dot plot is the part worth remembering. 16 of 18 participants expect at least one more increase before the end of 2026, and 10 of them don't see any cuts at all through 2029. Chair Kevin Warsh kept the explanations to a tight 130 words. In his view, inflation needs to come down.

Meanwhile, SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) stock is up 5% to $183.57. The Korean memory leader already dominates high-bandwidth memory, so a U.S. fab reads as insurance against tariffs and customer pressure rather than transformation for SK Hynix.

Ohio Talks Reignite Between Intel and SK Hynix

Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the discussions, that SK Hynix and Intel are weighing two structures: a lease of part of Intel's Ohio chipmaking complex, or a joint venture with Intel and major cloud computing firms to lock in memory supply. Neither company has confirmed a deal.

SK Hynix said it's exploring options to strengthen global competitiveness and that nothing has been finalized. Intel declined to comment on what it called speculation, while restating its commitment to preparing the Ohio site. The two statements leave room for the talks to advance or fade.

title: Qualcomm Faces Margin Pressure From Rising Costs: Can it Recover?
detail:
Qualcomm Faces Margin Pressure From Rising Costs: Can it Recover?
Zacks Equity Research
Thu, September 17, 2026 at 9:40 AM MDT 4 min read
QCOM
INTC
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM is facing near-term margin pressure as rising semiconductor input costs, weaker smartphone demand and an unfavorable product mix weigh on its QCT business. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, QCT EBT margin declined to 26% from 30% a year earlier. The company expects the metric to fall to 23-25% in the fiscal fourth quarter.

The primary pressure is coming from higher costs across the semiconductor supply chain. Qualcomm cited increases in wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, advanced packaging, memory and other materials, which are increasing product costs. QCOM is responding with a price hike. However, it has existing contracts with customers that have fixed prices; hence, it will take several quarters to get margin gains from those price increases.

Qualcomm is also dealing with a weaker mix within the premium handset market. Several handset OEMs are responding to the higher memory costs by changing chip selections and using prior-generation premium processors. This strategy can reduce the average value of the chip mix and put additional pressure on QCT margins.

QCT handset revenues fell 20% year over year to $5.09 billion in the fiscal third quarter as major OEMs reduced purchases. The handset weakness is particularly significant because declines in this business can outweigh growth in Qualcomm's newer markets. The company is seeing a faster reduction in Apple-related revenue. The company now expects its modem share in upcoming iPhone launches to be materially below its earlier 20% assumption. It forecasts Apple product revenue to decline about 50% sequentially from September to December 2026.

Higher operating expenses are adding to the pressure on profitability. The company is investing heavily in data-center products, AI computing and software. This may bring long-term benefits but increases costs in the near term. Management expects the margins to eventually recover once the pricing actions take effect.

How Are Competitors Faring?

Qualcomm faces competition from Intel Corporation INTC and Advanced Micro Devices AMD in the semiconductor space. At the end of the second quarter of 2026, Intel's Non-GAAP operating income was $2.77 billion against an operating loss of $0.5 billion in the year-ago quarter, with respective margins of 17.2% and a negative 3.9%. This is primarily backed by strong demand in several segments and cost discipline initiatives. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, Client Computing and Physical AI Group revenues rose 15% sequentially to $8.9 billion, with AI PC revenues rising 26% sequentially and representing about two-thirds of segment revenues. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, Data Center and AI revenues increased 24% sequentially and 59% year over year to $6.3 billion, while operating income rose by $1 billion sequentially to $2.5 billion.

AMD's Operating income jumped 245% to $3.09 billion, while operating margin widened 15 percentage points to 27%. Data Center operating income was $2.1 billion compared with a loss of $155 million in the year-ago quarter, translating into a 31% operating margin. Client and Gaming segment operating income declined 24% year over year to $582 million as higher expenses more than offset the revenue increase. Embedded operating income increased 40% year over year to $386 million. Operating margin improved to 40% from 33%, aided by higher sales and a favorable product mix. Management said embedded x86 products are becoming a meaningful growth driver as hyperscalers and networking customers adopt AMD CPUs for data center control functions.

title: Cerebras Drops 19% in 3 Months: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
detail:
Cerebras Drops 19% in 3 Months: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?

Cerebras Systems CBRS shares have dropped 19% in the past three months as profitability, margin pressure, heavy customer concentration, increasing spend on rapid infrastructure expansion and stiff competition continue to spook investors. CBRS' third-quarter 2026 core revenue guidance of $214-$216 million implies only about 2-3% sequential growth from the second quarter of 2026, which failed to impress investors. So, what should they do with the stock? Let's dig deep to find out.

Margin Compression to Hurt CBRS' Near-Term Prospects

Cerebras reported a GAAP net loss of $450.5 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $464.5 million in the first six months of the year. The company had an accumulated deficit of roughly $1.4 billion at the end of the second quarter of 2026 and expects expenses to remain elevated as it invests in research & development, cloud infrastructure and data-center capacity.

In the second quarter of 2026, core gross margin declined 590 basis points (bps) sequentially to 40.6% in the second quarter of 2026 as Cerebras temporarily rented systems back from customers to satisfy strong inference demand. The company expects the third quarter of 2026 to represent the trough, with core gross margin guided to 38-40%, while core operating margin is expected to deteriorate to negative 25-23% from negative 16% in the second quarter of 2026. Although management expects margins to recover as higher-cost rented capacity is replaced by Cerebras-owned systems, the near-term margin pressure likely tempered enthusiasm around the revenue outlook. For 2026, Cerebras now expects core gross margin between 41% and 43%, while operating margin is in the negative 19-17% range.

Cerebras is also perceived as risky by investors due to customer concentration and dependence on OpenAI. Revenues remain concentrated among a small number of customers as three customers individually represented 34%, 32% and 10% of second-quarter 2026 revenues, while a significant portion of Cerebras' $25.4 billion remaining performance obligations (RPO) is tied to its OpenAI agreement. The company acknowledged that OpenAI will remain a meaningful contributor in 2027, even though its share of revenues should decline as AWS and other customers scale.

Cerebras' prospects are suffering from stiff competition from the likes of NVIDIA NVDA, Advanced Micro Devices AMD and Intel INTC in the AI space. NVIDIA is dominating the AI GPU market through its Blackwell, Hopper and DGX/NVL systems that are used for AI training and inference. AMD's MI300 and MI350 accelerator families are competing with CBRS in hyperscale AI infrastructure and enterprise AI clusters. Meanwhile, Intel's Gaudi AI accelerators target enterprise AI training and inference as a lower-cost GPU alternative. Shares of NVIDIA have risen 1.5%, while AMD and Intel dropped 4.6% and 24.6%, respectively.
